title: Pushing the Frontier of Full-Song Generation
hook: Full, multi-minute songs from just lyrics and a text prompt: a two-stage system plans the song autoregressively, then renders it with flow matching for high-fidelity audio.
key_points: One framework, three tasks: lyrics-to-song, instrumental-only generation, and cover generation that restyles a song while keeping its melody.
A semantic-aware tokenizer compresses audio into 8-codebook residual vector-quantized (RVQ) tokens.
A hierarchical autoregressive language model plans the full song over those tokens; a diffusion-style module (FullDiT) then flow-matches high-fidelity audio in a continuous VAE latent space.
Cover generation uses a two-level melody module that extracts and discretizes melody cues from a reference track.
Reward-based post-training (DPO, GRPO, OPD; flow-based GRPO for the renderer) lifts musicality — competitive on a multilingual benchmark and the Artificial Analysis vocals leaderboard.
content_html: Generating a short musical clip is one thing; producing a coherent, multi-minute song with vocals, structure, and lyrics is much harder. This technical report presents a unified framework that does exactly that from lyrics, text descriptions, and musical attributes.
extra_html:
Plan, then render

The system supports three tasks — lyrics-to-song, instrumental-only generation, and cover generation. Under the hood it separates planning from rendering. A semantic-aware tokenizer first compresses audio into 8-codebook residual vector-quantized (RVQ) tokens. A hybrid autoregressive language model then performs hierarchical planning over those tokens to lay out the whole song, and FullDiT — a flow-matching module operating in a continuous VAE latent space, conditioned on the tokens, lyrics, and text captions — renders high-fidelity audio.

Melody control and reward tuning

For covers, a two-level melody module extracts and discretizes melody cues from a reference track so the output preserves the original tune in a new style. The authors apply reward-based post-training — DPO, GRPO, and OPD for the planner, and flow-based GRPO for FullDiT — to improve musicality and rendering. On a multilingual automatic benchmark and the Artificial Analysis "Music with Vocals" leaderboard, the framework achieves competitive results. Dai et al., arXiv 2026.

related.title: MusicGen: Simple and Controllable Music Generation
related.hook: Generate music from a text description or a melody reference using a single autoregressive transformer over discrete audio tokens - no cascade of specialized models required.

related.title: Stereo2Spatial: Upmixing Stereo Music to 7.1.4 Spatial Audio with Flow-Matching Diffusion
related.hook: A hobbyist project trains a flow-matching diffusion model to turn ordinary stereo music into full 7.1.4 spatial mixes — built on a dedicated VAE latent space rather than working directly on audio.

flashcards.explanation_html: The hybrid autoregressive LM does hierarchical planning over RVQ tokens; FullDiT then flow-matches audio in a continuous VAE latent space to improve fidelity.

flashcards.prompt: What does the semantic-aware tokenizer produce, and why?
flashcards.back_html: It encodes audio into 8-codebook RVQ (residual vector-quantized) tokens — a compact discrete representation the autoregressive model can plan a full song over efficiently.

flashcards.prompt: How does the system generate a cover of an existing song?
flashcards.back_html: A two-level melody module extracts and discretizes melody cues from the reference audio, guiding generation so the new version keeps the original's melodic content in a different style.
